which_scoreboard: THE LAB, and the pool is expected to SIT STILL. Said before the run, with the reason: the defect needs a body to owe a recharge AND be asleep, frozen, flinched, confused, attracted or paralysed on the SAME turn. Two uncommon states at once. There is no cause row in `data/verification/longtail-C-poltergeist.json` that names a recharge at all - the only `|cant|` rows are three paralysis ones and a sleep cure - so I have NO evidence the pool contains a single instance.

prediction.reasoning: FLAT ON BOTH. This is the deliberate obscure-tail case Will's 2026-08-23 ruling covers: the roster and the census carry it, the pinned pool is not where it lives. A pool that moves at all would be a surprise and I would go looking for WHICH game before claiming it.

counters.MEDSEEN.rechargeSpentAtBeforeMove: > 0 over 961 games - Hyper Beam is 1,627 corpus clicks, so recharges certainly happen; this is the road they must now come down
counters.MEDSEEN.rechargeSpentOffMove: expected 0. The authority never offers a switch or a pass to a locked body (`onLockMove: 'recharge'` -> `trapped: true`), so a non-zero means the DRIVER handed this engine an action the format cannot produce.

how_a_miss_would_read: if either figure moves, the co-occurrence is NOT as rare as this reasoning says and the moved games must be named by cause before anything is claimed. A figure that gets WORSE means hoisting the refusal above the status chain took a turn away from a body the authority lets act - most likely the Destiny Bond ordering or a `sleepUsable` move (Sleep Talk / Snore), which run AFTER their own `|cant|slp` and would now never be reached on a recharging body. That pairing is impossible in the authority for the same reason (the request offers only `recharge`), but it is the shape to check first.
